extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A subset of 23 particularly challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which no prior result from Srivastava et al. (2022) has outperformed the average human-rater score.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.citeAs: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, and Jason Wei. 2022. Challenging BIG-Bench tasks and whether chain-of-thought can solve them. arXiv:2210.09261v1 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated by filtering BIG-Bench tasks using explicit criteria and then selecting the remaining 23 tasks; for most tasks, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some BIG-Bench tasks lacked metadata such as human baselines, and some had only the minimum number of examples needed to qualify for submission.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source was BIG-Bench, specifically tasks from the BIG-Bench benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks were filtered to those with three or fewer subtasks, at least 103 examples, human-rater baselines, and multiple-choice or exact-match evaluation metrics; tasks where the best reported model beat the average human-rater score and tasks outside scope were removed. For all but three tasks, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually wrote chain-of-thought exemplars for each BBH task, composing three chain-of-thought exemplars per task and prepending "let’s think step-by-step" to all CoT annotations in the few-shot exemplars.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Final answers were extracted based on expected keywords such as "the answer is," and accuracy was measured using exact match against ground-truth labels.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper cautions that surpassing average human-rater performance on these tasks should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some tasks require common practices and presuppositions in Western society, and the reported human-rater scores are not representative of the entire population.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human-rater scores are not fully representative of human performance; task formatting and content changed over time; raters solved subsampled evaluation sets with limited time and could use external resources; some task descriptions were hard to follow. The authors also excluded some tasks as outside scope because they required specialized knowledge or were not worth attempting with chain-of-thought.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is an evaluation benchmark for measuring language model capabilities and limitations on challenging tasks, and the released data, prompts, and model outputs are intended to facilitate further research.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Human-Rater Baseline Performance. Finally, we note that even though Srivastava et al. (2022) report the average and maximum of human-rater performances on most BIG-Bench tasks; the organizers acknowledge that one should be careful in interpreting these results because the scores are not fully representative of human performance. The human-evaluation component of the benchmark took almost a year, during which the formatting and content of some tasks had been changed multiple times. Human-raters were allocated a few hours per day to solve a sub-sampled evaluation set of a benchmark task, where they could use extemal resources such as the Intemet. In some cases, the task description was hard to follow and could have been better-formulated.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: BIG-Bench is a collaborative benchmark that aims to quantitatively measure the capabilities and limitations of language models ... We release the data and prompts used in the work, as well as the outputs from the Codex models, to facilitate further research.
